The new rules from the Lost Valley review (docs/COURSE-DESIGN.md, "Story, features and fairway structure"): every hole built round a story, a feature of its own seen from the tee; vary how the fairways are put together (split, broken by a cross hazard, stepping down, an island), no more than two or three plain single fairways a nine and never two of a kind in a row; big sand now and then. Each hole page now opens with its story in one line and its structure.

Review of round 3. Every hole already had its feature (the kipuka, the barranco, the crater, the tube's bridge, the drop off the Notch, the columns, the lavafall, the lake, the island), so the stories mostly stand. What fell short: seven par 4s and 5s with five plain single fairways (1, 2, 7, 8 and 9 only bent or tapered), 1 and 2 plain in a row, and no big sand anywhere.

2 The Barranco: broken by a cross bunker. A band of black ash sand, the floods' channel, runs right across the fairway on the climb, 75–90 m short of the green (it replaces the approach bunker). It sits on the second shot, well past where any tee set's drive finishes.

3 The Cinder Cone: a green in a ring of sand. Ash sand wraps the green 2–3 m off its edge on every side but the front, so the only way on that misses the sand is up the middle through the breach. The two pot bunkers go.

7 The Lavafall: broken by a lava rill. The overflow: the fall's pool spills back down the bay along the wall on the left and cuts across the fairway on a diagonal at the foot of the ledge, 330–350 m out (nearest on the right). Lay up short of it at about 310 m, or carry it into the bay with the second; the long cinder bunker down the left gives way to the rill. It's a stroke and a drop, like all lava, and it stays 56 m or more from the 8th's tees.

9 The Heart: split round a tumulus, then the bridge. Where drives land a tumulus (a blister of old lava, rock with boulders round it) splits the shore fairway: the left lane wide and away from the lava but longer, with the bridge out of line; the beach lane by the lava, straight onto the bridge. Each lane is 26 m or more at every tee set's drive; the check now measures each lane of a split. Down the right a black-sand beach runs 160 m between the fairway and the lava (it replaces the catch bunker).

8 The Lake stays a single fairway (one of two, with the 1st), and I tried a split here first: the lake's pit bank leaves no room for a second lane. Instead a hornito, a steaming spatter chimney, stands on the crest's left shoulder as the marker to aim by from the blind tee.

Structures now: 1 single, dogleg left · 2 broken by a cross bunker · 3 a green in a ring of sand · 4 over the tube's trench on a bridge · 5 all carry off the rim · 6 stepping down a crag · 7 broken by a lava rill · 8 single, cape over a crest · 9 split, then a bridge to an island. Big sand: a cross bunker (2), a ring round a green (3) and a fairway-long beach (9), once each.
Checks: every check passes (pins, tees, tips spots, landings, leans, green contour). Routing, yardages, greens and tees are unchanged.
